state.durability_stakes: Every retired port must rerun on demand at F01, and only fulfilled obligations count toward the 28. A probe that needs an idle machine converts each future rerun into a scheduling puzzle and trains the team to distrust red. With three workers the 256 GB host holds load 40-60+ for hours; calm stretches appear only around solitary light tasks.
state.load_evidence: The worker's rc=0 over 27 checks consumed 38 minutes in calm air, with its own note that every delivery burns about 7.6 CPU-s against an unyielding 5s mail deadline, viable only at load 35-40 or under. Coordinator attempts at 60+ load died twice in stage (code 10) and once in spawn (code 20) after 43m34s. Both sides agree the build is 124/124 independent of load.
state.mandate: AI agents author this language and no legacy artifact is owed survival; the operating rule favors arriving at the goal over accumulating scaffolding or proof strata. tests/auth_signup/probe.py plus tests/auth_signup/fake_mail.py already gave way at 5ec1cdb to tests/auth_signup/probe/. What remains is deciding whether that live probe gets reworked or gets a documented envelope.
state.production_timing: Production delivery is sub-second work; the 30s baseline allowance per phase group was slack that never mattered. The 7.6 CPU-s figure is toolchain ignition per `canlc run` sender launch, unrelated to mail speed in production. So the 5s deadline in the probe clocks harness startup while the judged property, an authentic delivery present in the mailbox, has no clock in it.
